speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you tell me how long you've had the swelling in your right knee and if you experienced any recent injuries?

speaker: Patient
text: 18-month-old boy. The patient is brought in by his parents due to swelling in his right knee noticed after playing in the park. The parents report that there was no obvious injury or incident at the park that could have led to the swelling. Upon further questioning, the mother recalls that an uncle on her side of the family had similar problems, suggesting a possible genetic component.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the knee feel hot to the touch, and is he having difficulty bearing weight on it? Has he ever had similar swelling in other joints, such as his elbows or ankles?

text: My main symptom is Swelling of the right knee. I also have No recent trauma or injury, Familial history of similar symptoms.

The normal Factor VIII and IX levels rule out Hemophilia A and B, so I need to investigate other causes for the bleeding tendency. Have you noticed any bleeding after vaccinations or minor cuts, and does he have a history of joint pain or swelling in other areas?

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal Factor XI and platelet function tests further reduce the likelihood of a common hereditary bleeding disorder.
